questions.stem: In an environmental management system, which pair correctly identifies an aspect and an impact?
options: Air contamination is the aspect; solvent use is the impact
An audit is the aspect; a procedure is the impact
A permit is the aspect; a budget is the impact
Solvent use is an aspect; air contamination is a potential impact
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An aspect is an element of activities, products, or services that can interact with the environment; an impact is the resulting change.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This reverses the activity or element and its environmental consequence.
Audits and procedures are management tools, not the stated aspect-impact relationship.
Permits and budgets are controls and resources, not this environmental cause-effect pair.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34 and Chapter 31, environmental management and ISO 14001 concepts, pp. 754-778 and 723-727

questions.stem: A federal agency proposes a major action with potentially significant environmental effects. Which process may be required before the decision?
options: Environmental review that may include an environmental assessment or environmental impact statement
An OSHA 300A posting only
A workers compensation premium audit
A confined-space entry permit
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: NEPA integrates environmental information into federal agency planning and decision-making, including appropriate public and alternatives review.
incorrectOptionExplanations: OSHA injury summaries do not evaluate environmental consequences of federal actions.
Insurance review is unrelated to NEPA decision-making.
A confined-space permit controls a specific entry, not federal environmental review.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34, NEPA requirements and process, pp. 754-758

questions.stem: A production increase may raise emissions above the assumptions used in an air permit. What should occur before the change?
options: Run at the higher rate and check annual totals later
Evaluate permit and regulatory implications and obtain required approval before operating the change
Treat the change as a maintenance decision only
Ignore emissions if no odor is detected
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Environmental compliance should be integrated into change control so approvals, limits, monitoring, and records are addressed before operation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Post-change review can result in unauthorized operation.
Production and emission changes may trigger regulatory and management-of-change review.
Odor is not a reliable measure of regulated emissions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34, Clean Air Act permits and enforcement, pp. 770-778; Chapter 38 MOC

questions.stem: A process intermittently sends a high-strength contaminant slug to wastewater treatment. Which control is strongest?
options: Increase sampling only after the discharge
Dilute the slug with clean water
Control or segregate the source and equalize the flow before it reaches treatment
Ignore the variation if the monthly average is acceptable
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Source reduction, segregation, containment, and flow equalization prevent shock loading and protect treatment performance.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Sampling detects the event but does not prevent treatment upset.
Dilution does not reduce pollutant mass and can increase hydraulic loading.
Short-term loadings can disrupt treatment and violate instantaneous or daily limits.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34, pollution prevention and water-management concepts, pp. 754-778

questions.stem: A tank is near soil drains that connect to surface water. What should the environmental risk assessment emphasize?
options: Only tank purchase price
Only the color of the stored liquid
Only the number of employees nearby
Source, release mechanism, migration pathway, receptors, and controls
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Environmental risk follows the chain from source through transport media to human or ecological receptors and available barriers.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Cost does not characterize environmental fate and exposure.
Color does not determine migration or ecological consequence.
Workers are important receptors, but environmental pathways and off-site receptors also require analysis.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34, environmental policy, waste, air, and water controls, pp. 754-778

questions.stem: Why do universal-waste rules exist for specified common hazardous wastes?
options: To streamline collection and management while maintaining environmental protection
To declare every listed material nonhazardous
To allow disposal in ordinary trash without conditions
To remove all state regulatory authority
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The streamlined framework encourages proper collection and recycling of common waste streams such as certain batteries, lamps, and equipment.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The materials remain subject to management standards.
Universal-waste rules do not authorize unconditional ordinary disposal.
Authorized states may have additional or more stringent requirements.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 34, RCRA and universal waste, pp. 758-764

questions.stem: What is the best way for a multisite organization to keep environmental obligations current?
options: Use one old permit as the only reference for every site
Maintain a site-specific legal register with owners, applicability reviews, changes, and compliance evidence
Rely on employee memory
Review regulations only after an enforcement action
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A controlled obligations process links applicable requirements to responsible owners, operating controls, monitoring, and periodic evaluation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Site processes, permits, jurisdictions, and conditions differ and change.
Memory is not controlled or auditable evidence.
Reactive review exposes the organization to preventable noncompliance.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 31, 34, and 37, management systems, environmental law, and compliance auditing

questions.stem: A reportable chemical release may have crossed the property boundary. What is the safest compliance approach?
options: Wait for a complaint before evaluating reporting
Notify only the company insurer
Activate the response plan and promptly evaluate all applicable notification duties using verified quantity and timing information
Assume local fire department notification satisfies every law
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Release response should pair immediate protective actions with a documented applicability and notification determination.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Reporting clocks may run before off-site complaints occur.
Insurance notification does not replace regulatory and community obligations.
Different laws and agencies can impose separate notifications.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 27, 34, and 39, hazardous releases and emergency management, pp. 616-634, 754-778, and 870-889

questions.stem: Which environmental objective is best written?
options: Reduce environmental impacts whenever practical and review them during annual planning
Eliminate every environmental problem immediately regardless of technical feasibility
Encourage employees to choose greener practices without defining a measurable result
Cut hazardous solvent use per production unit 20% by year-end and verify progress monthly
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A useful objective defines the outcome, baseline or metric, target, timeframe, ownership, and verification method.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This is not specific, measurable, assigned, or time-bound.
The statement is absolute and does not define controllable performance or measurement.
A general request does not establish a managed objective.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 31, 33, and 34, management systems, sustainability KPIs, and environmental management

questions.stem: Monitoring confirms a permit limit exceedance. What response is strongest?
options: Control the release, make required notifications, investigate causes, correct the system, and verify effectiveness
Delete the data point as an outlier
Repeat the sample until a lower value appears
Wait for the annual audit
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A robust response protects receptors, meets notification duties, preserves data, addresses root causes, and prevents recurrence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Removing valid adverse data is unethical and can violate record requirements.
Resampling does not erase the original exceedance and may delay response.
Immediate control and reporting duties cannot wait for a scheduled audit.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
